name: Python Foundations
description: Write Python you can trust: core types, functions, modules, classes and simple tests.

lessonNames.l4-one-line-lists: Building a list in one line
lessonNames.l13-one-at-a-time: Producing values one at a time

lessonObjectives.l1-why-not-0-3: Explain floating point error and compare floats safely with a tolerance.
lessonObjectives.l2-slicing: Index and slice lists, including negative indices and steps.
lessonObjectives.l3-unpacking: Use tuples and unpack values in assignments and loops.
lessonObjectives.l4-one-line-lists: Write list comprehensions, with and without a condition.
lessonObjectives.l5-lookup-by-name: Store and look up values by key in a dictionary.
lessonObjectives.l6-membership: Use a set to remove duplicates and to test membership quickly.
lessonObjectives.l7-arguments: Write functions with default and keyword arguments, and avoid the mutable default trap.
lessonObjectives.l8-who-changes-the-list: Predict when a function changes the object you passed it.
lessonObjectives.l9-splitting-files: Import from your own modules and from the standard library.
lessonObjectives.l10-reading-a-csv: Read a CSV file of prices with the `csv` module.
lessonObjectives.l11-when-things-go-wrong: Raise and catch exceptions on purpose, and only the ones you expect.
lessonObjectives.l12-data-with-behaviour: Write a small class with an initialiser and methods.
lessonObjectives.l13-one-at-a-time: Write a generator and use it in a loop.
lessonObjectives.l14-sorting-by-what-matters: Sort with key functions and lambdas.
lessonObjectives.l15-checking-your-code: Write assertions that test a function’s edge cases.
lessonObjectives.l16-returns-from-a-file: Compute daily returns from a CSV of prices in plain Python, and turn the script into a tool (argv, main guard, results file).
